Phone Recorder user guide

Phone Recorder records phone calls over Bluetooth for podcasts. Your computer connects to the phone the way a car kit does, so any call on the phone comes through the app: normal calls and calling apps such as WhatsApp or Signal. The caller and every microphone are recorded on separate tracks, and all of them are also available to OBS.

1. What you need

  • A Linux computer with PipeWire (standard on current distributions).
  • A Bluetooth adapter. A separate USB dongle is best, because the app takes full control of the adapter it uses: other Bluetooth devices on that adapter (headphones, mouse, keyboard) disconnect while the app runs. A cheap, well-supported choice is the TP-Link UB500. The built-in adapter works too. See the hardware table in the README.
  • Headphones for monitoring. With speakers the caller may hear an echo (there is an echo canceller for that case, see the mixer).
  • One-time setup (asks for your password): This lets your user drive USB Bluetooth adapters without root rights. Building and installing the app is described in BUILD.md.
    scripts/install-udev-rule.sh

About sound quality

Bluetooth calls are limited by the phone link itself, no matter what the app records at:

Shown during the callSample rateTypical phones
CVSD, narrowband8 kHzold phones or adapters
mSBC, HD voice16 kHzmost phones from the last decade
LC3-SWB, super wideband32 kHznewer phones

The app picks the best one the phone and the adapter both support. Your own microphones are recorded at full quality (48 kHz, 32-bit).

2. First start: choose the Bluetooth adapter

On the first start the app asks which Bluetooth adapter to use.

  1. Pick your adapter. Each entry shows the chip, the USB ID and whether the system uses it right now.
  2. Optional: open the entry to choose the Mode:
    • Direct USB (recommended): the app talks to the adapter itself and loads its firmware.
    • Kernel driver, raw access: for chips whose firmware only the Linux kernel can load (MediaTek, Intel AX210 and newer, Qualcomm). Needs the helper: run scripts/setup-userchan-helper.sh once.
  3. Choose Use this adapter. If the system is using it, the app first warns that other Bluetooth devices on it will disconnect. The app then restarts once.

While the app runs, that adapter belongs to the app. When you close the app, it is given back to the system, also if the app should ever crash.

To switch adapters later: Menu (☰), Choose Bluetooth adapter.

3. Pair your phone

  1. In the Phone section, turn on Pairing mode.
  2. On the phone, open the Bluetooth settings and choose the app's name (by default "Phone Recorder", see Bluetooth name).
  3. The app shows a code. Check that the phone shows the same code, then choose Pair on both the phone and the computer.

Older phones may ask for a PIN instead. Type the same PIN on both sides, for example 0000:

After pairing, the phone appears under Paired phones. Next time it connects by itself when the app starts (or use Connect in the list). Forget (the bin icon) removes a phone; it must then be paired again.

Bluetooth name

The name phones see can be changed in the Phone section: select the Bluetooth name field, type a new name and press Enter. It changes right away. Phones that are already paired may show the old name until they connect again.

4. The main window

  • Header bar: Record / Stop with the recording time, Marker, Add input and the main menu (☰). The subtitle shows the Bluetooth status.
  • Left side: the current call, Make a call, the Phone section (connection, battery, signal, Bluetooth name, pairing mode) and Paired phones.
  • Right side: the Mixer with one strip per source and the Outputs section.
  • Status line at the bottom: free disk space with the recording time left, an audio health indicator ("no dropouts" or a count) and where the current recording is saved.

5. Calls

  • Incoming call: the call card shows the caller's name or number and Answer and Decline (Ctrl+Shift+A, Ctrl+Shift+H). If the window is in the background, a desktop notification with an Answer button appears.
  • Make a call: type the number under Make a call and press Enter or Call. Redial calls the last number again. The Keypad sends tones during a call (for menus like "press 1").
  • During the call: the card shows the call time and the codec, for example "mSBC, HD voice (16 kHz)". Hang up ends the call.
  • Call audio on the phone or the computer: Move call audio to the phone hands the audio back to the handset (the call continues); Move call audio to the computer brings it back (Ctrl+Shift+T). The app brings the audio to the computer by itself when a call starts.
  • Call waiting: if a second call comes in during a call, Answer puts the current call on hold and takes the new one; Decline rejects only the new call.

Closing the app during a call does not end the call; it continues on the phone.

6. The mixer

Each source has a strip. The Caller strip is always first.

ControlWhat it does
Name (click to rename)Used for the recording file and the OBS source name.
Input deviceWhich microphone or input the strip uses. "System default input" follows your desktop setting.
Level meter and numberPeak level. Aim for about -12 dB when speaking. "CLIP" means too loud: turn the volume down.
Volume sliderGain of the strip, -30 to +24 dB.
Left-right sliderPosition in the stereo mix.
MuteTakes the strip out of the mix and the call. Its own OBS source and recording track keep the sound.
SoloListen only to soloed strips on the monitor. Changes nothing in the recording, the call or OBS.
In call / Not in callWhether the caller hears this input. It never removes the input from OBS or the recording.
Low cutRemoves rumble and handling noise below 80 Hz.
GateTurns the strip down when nobody speaks into it.
RemoveRemoves the input (not possible while recording).

The caller is never sent back to the phone, so the caller never hears an echo of themselves. This is called a mix-minus.

Add input (Ctrl+I) adds another microphone or input, for example a music player you want on its own track.

Outputs

  • Meters: full mix (left and right), what is sent to the caller, and the monitor.
  • Monitor (headphones): turn on, choose the output device and set its volume. The monitor plays the full mix, or only the soloed strips.
  • Level sent to the caller: overall volume of what the caller hears.
  • Echo cancelling: only needed when the caller is played on speakers.

7. Recording

  • Press Record (Ctrl+R) to start and Stop to finish. A message tells you where the recording was saved, with an Open folder button.
  • Each recording gets its own folder, named by date and time, for example ~/Music/Podcast recordings/2026-11-10_14-30-00/.
  • Inside are one file per source, all exactly in step:
    01-full-mix.wav        the stereo mix
02-caller.wav          the caller
03-host.wav            each input, named after its strip
04-co-host.wav
markers-audacity.txt   markers for Audacity (File, Import, Labels)
chapters.txt           markers as chapter times
  • Markers (Ctrl+M or F9) mark a point in the recording, for example a good quote. They are stored in the WAV files as cue points, as an Audacity label file and as a chapter list.
  • Automatic recording: in Preferences, recording can start by itself when a call starts and stop when it ends.
  • Recordings are safe if the computer crashes or loses power: the files stay readable up to the last moment.
  • The status line warns when less than 15 minutes of disk space are left.

Inputs cannot be added or removed while recording.

8. Preferences

Open with Menu (☰), Preferences or Ctrl+comma.

Recording

  • Recording folder.
  • File format: WAV 32-bit float (best for editing, default), WAV 24-bit, FLAC 24-bit (lossless, about half the size) or Opus (small, for sharing).
  • Start recording when a call starts and Stop automatic recordings when the call ends.

Audio

  • Protect the full mix from clipping: a gentle limiter on the stereo mix. Single-input tracks are never limited.

Bluetooth

  • Bluetooth name (changes right away).
  • HD voice and Super wideband: allow the better codecs. Leave on.
  • Ask the phone to skip its own noise reduction: your microphones are already clean, so the caller hears you more naturally.
  • Secure Connections: turn off only if pairing or call audio fails with an older adapter.
  • Extra firmware folder: for adapters whose firmware is not in the system.
  • Save Bluetooth trace: for troubleshooting (see below).

Apart from the name, these take effect after a restart.

OBS

See the OBS guide.

Language and accessibility

  • Language of the app: System default, English or Norsk bokmål. Takes effect after a restart; the message that appears has a Restart now button.
  • Text size: 100 to 200 percent, on top of your desktop setting.

9. Keyboard shortcuts

Press F1 (or Ctrl+?) to see them in the app.

KeysAction
Ctrl+RStart or stop recording
Ctrl+M or F9Add a marker
Ctrl+Shift+AAnswer
Ctrl+Shift+HDecline or hang up
Ctrl+Shift+TMove call audio between phone and computer
Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9Input 1 to 9: heard by the caller on or off
Alt+1 to Alt+9Input 1 to 9: mute on or off
Ctrl+IAdd an input
Ctrl+commaPreferences
Ctrl+plus, Ctrl+minus, Ctrl+0Larger, smaller, normal text
F10Main menu
Ctrl+QQuit

Everything else works with Tab, Shift+Tab, the arrow keys, Enter, Space and Esc.

10. Accessibility and language

  • Every control has a name for screen readers, and important events are read out: incoming calls, call connected and ended, recording started and stopped, pairing codes.
  • Nothing depends on colour alone: switches show text and icons, meters show numbers.
  • Text size and language are in Preferences (see above).
  • The full statement, in English and Norwegian, is in ACCESSIBILITY.md.

11. Troubleshooting

ProblemWhat to do
The phone does not find the appTurn on Pairing mode, then search again on the phone.
"The chosen Bluetooth adapter was not found"Plug the adapter in, or choose another one in Choose Bluetooth adapter.
"Adapter failed"Save an adapter report (Menu, Save adapter report) and try the other mode for the adapter, or another adapter.
A call connects but no audio arrivesThe app says so. In kernel driver mode, try Direct USB. Otherwise try another adapter.
Only narrowband (8 kHz)The adapter or the phone has no wideband support. Try another adapter.
The caller hears an echoUse headphones, or turn on Echo cancelling.
Clicks or dropoutsThe status line counts them. Close heavy programs; check the disk is not full.
Bluetooth is still gone from the system after the app closed (rare)Run bt-phone-recorder --release-adapters.

For a detailed problem report:

  1. Turn on Preferences, Bluetooth, Save Bluetooth trace and restart the app.
  2. Reproduce the problem.
  3. Use Menu, Save adapter report, and attach it together with the newest .pklg file from ~/.local/state/bt-phone-recorder/ (it opens in Wireshark).

12. Where files are stored

PathContents
~/Music/Podcast recordings/your recordings (changeable)
~/.config/bt-phone-recorder/settings and remembered phone names
~/.local/share/bt-phone-recorder/pairing keys
~/.local/state/bt-phone-recorder/log file and Bluetooth traces
~/.cache/bt-phone-recorder/unpacked Bluetooth firmware (recreated when needed)
